{{short description|American mathematician}}
{{BLP sources|date=May 2018}}
'''Frank Deutsch''' (born December 18, 1936) is an American academic [[applied mathematician]] specializing in [[approximation theory]]. He is an emeritus professor at [[The Pennsylvania State University]],<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.math.psu.edu/directory/department.php|title=Full Department Directory - Department of Mathematics|website=Math.psu.edu|accessdate=9 May 2018}}</ref> and is the author of over 94 journal articles and two books,<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.math.psu.edu/deutsch/dp1.html |title=Archived copy |access-date=2013-05-02 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131209103401/http://www.math.psu.edu/deutsch/dp1.html |archive-date=2013-12-09 |url-status=dead }}</ref> and on the editorial board of five journals.

He earned the B.S. in [[Mechanical Engineering]] from the [[University of Hartford]] (1960), the M.S. in [[Mathematics]] from [[Northwestern University]] (1961), and the Ph.D. in Applied Mathematics from Brown University (1966)<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.math.psu.edu/deutsch/ |title=Archived copy |access-date=2013-05-02 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130504181556/http://www.math.psu.edu/deutsch/ |archive-date=2013-05-04 |url-status=dead }}</ref> under [[Philip J. Davis]].
